newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's CIS issues $12-mln Senior, Junior notes.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's CIS issues $12-mln Senior, Junior notes.

text.p: Beirut's Capital Investment Services (CIS) finance house said on Monday it closed a $12 million issue of Senior and Junior Notes linked to six-month Lebanese treasury bills.

The issue, the second biggest under a $100-million programme launched in May 1994, brought the total to date to over $76 million. It follows a $23.275 million issue of senior and junior notes in September linked to two-year t-bills.
"We successfully closed the eighth series today," CIS Treasurer Thierry Depolla said in a statement, adding it comprised $8 million in Senior Notes and $4 million in Junior Notes.
"The Notes are issued against six-month treasuries of the Lebanese Republic denominated in Lebanese pounds and currently yielding 16.48 percent per annum," he added.
Most of the earlier issues were made against one-year treasury bills, Depolla said.

Annual interest on the Senior Notes is 10.25 percent. The Junior Notes carry no fixed interest but are leveraged against the pound's exchange rate against the dollar, with returns based on the local currency's performance versus the U.S. currency.
Indicated return at a constant exchange rate over six months would be 17.31 percent per annum, Depolla said.

The pound has steadily appreciated since billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri assumed power in late 1992 with a mandate to rebuild Lebanon from the 1975-90 civil war. The pound, which hit a low of 2,750 to the dollar in mid-1992, closed on Monday at 1,553.75.
Depolla said there was substantial interest from foreign institutional investors in the Notes.
"Foreign institutional investors took more than half the issue, about one third went to expatriate Lebanese and the rest to local investors," he told Reuters.
"This was a clear sign of confidence in Lebanon's political and economic stability," he added.
The issuer is Lebanese Securities Inc, a special purpose company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands solely for the purpose of issuing the notes.
CIS is arranger, servicer and placement agent for the programme. The Royal Bank of Canada Trust Corporation Ltd is trustee while the paying agent is Royal Bank of Canada, London Branch.
